artifacts.summary: Research for a durable lint (lint-test-root-resolution.sh) closing the invocation-path-dependent repo-root walk-up class: names the exact model (lint-test-harness-adoption.sh), the sanctioned/forbidden discriminator, the one known false-positive case needing an allowlist entry, and three newly-found live violation instances to fix before the lint lands.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's shell test-suite corpus, a fixed-depth repo-root walk-up (`cd "$DIR/../../../.."`) is SANCTIONED only when it sits behind a git-first (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) or validated-candidate (check the resolved path exists/matches a sentinel before accepting it) guard; it is FORBIDDEN as the sole, unconditional computation because source-store vs. deployed invocation paths differ in nesting depth. This rule (settled by task 589's plan Non-Goals) is the detection rule for a planned lint-test-root-resolution.sh modeled on lint-test-harness-adoption.sh.

lint-test-harness-adoption.sh (agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/lint/) is a reusable structural template for a new corpus-wide shell lint: shared test-file scan-scope definition (tests/ dir or test- prefix, matching script-inventory.sh's classification), line-oriented regex detection with a documented KNOWN LIMITATION, --verbose/--help/[path...] usage, exit 0/1/2, and a per-path:line directly-inspected ALLOWLIST array for confirmed false positives. It is itself NOT wired into verify-deploy.sh/gate-registry.data as a deploy gate -- only a standalone script with its own sibling fixture test (test-lint-test-harness-adoption.sh, classified unit).
